=== SHARED CONTEXT (identical in every M3 task prompt; read it all) ===

PROJECT. SXC-1 Trainer: an interactive training course for the Casio SXC-1 sampler,
written entirely in Haskell (Miso + GHC WASM), compiled to WebAssembly, served as
static files from GitHub Pages. Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1.
No backend, no network writes, no analytics. The tree is at tag `m2`: the manual
reader (M1) and the exercise engine (M2) are shipped and gate-cleared.

BUILD / CHECK.
  . "$HOME/.ghc-wasm/env"                       # activates the toolchain
  cd /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site
  wasm32-wasi-cabal build -j2 exe:app           # SXC1_JOBS>2 can OOM this machine
  ./scripts/build-site.sh                       # assembles site/public/
  ./scripts/check-site.sh                       # the full gate suite
Run checker binaries with `wasm-run.mjs <binary> <args>` after sourcing the env.
`wasm-run.mjs` is on PATH from the toolchain env; the absolute path is
$HOME/.ghc-wasm/wasm-run/bin/wasm-run.mjs.

THE SIZE CEILING IS THE DEFINING CONSTRAINT OF M3.
`scripts/check-site.sh` carries `WASM_GZIP_CEILING_BYTES=1000000` and fails the
build if `gzip -c site/public/app.wasm | wc -c` reaches it. M2 shipped at 988,367
bytes -- 11,633 bytes of headroom. **NO M3 TASK MAY EDIT THAT CONSTANT.** Raising a
tripwire instead of fitting under it is a failure mode this project has been burned
by twice; the ceiling is a coordinator decision at a gate, never a task's.

Measured budget facts (from the M3 designer's probes; see briefs/M3-plan.md
appendix -- these are measurements, not estimates):
  * splitting the validating parser out of exe:app saves 45,878 gzip bytes
  * INDEX-driven compile-time embedding saves a further 3,879
  * the M3 progress engine costs +34,123 for ~530 app-linked lines (~64 B/line)
  * embedded .ex.md content costs 0.3456 gzip bytes per raw byte
Each task carries its own descending byte budget in its verify commands. If you
cannot fit, STOP AND REPORT -- do not enable --optimize, do not edit the ceiling,
do not delete checks.

CODE-SIZE LADDER (inherited from M2, still binding on anything linked into exe:app):
derive `Eq` only on wide record/sum types -- NO derived `Show` (hand-write the small
renderer a diagnostic needs anyway); reuse `SXC1.Content.Stats.jsonEscape` and
`Exercises.Corpus`'s jStr/jArr/jInt/jInteger/jKV/jObj/jBool combinators rather than
writing a second JSON encoder; keep `-O1`; never pass `--optimize` to build-site.sh.
There is no `-split-sections` in the cabal file, so a module links as ONE ATOMIC
UNIT: importing any name from a module drags in that module's every other
definition, including derived instances on types you never touch. That single fact
is why the reader/validator split exists.

CLOCK DISCIPLINE (from the M2 gate, non-negotiable and extended by M3).
`SXC1.Exercise.Engine` defines `newtype MonoMs = MonoMs Integer` and
`newtype WallMs = WallMs Integer` -- deliberately distinct newtypes over the same
representation so the two clock domains cannot be swapped at a call site. MonoMs is
monotonic and is the ONLY thing safe to subtract for a duration; WallMs is a
wall-clock epoch reading and is the only thing safe to schedule a date against.
Neither derives Num or Ord, so they cannot be arithmetic-mixed. Pure code NEVER
reads a clock: every clock reading is taken at the IO boundary and passed in as an
argument. M3 extends this -- nothing under `SXC1.Progress.*` may read a clock,
import Miso, or perform IO.

THE M2 CONTRACT M3 BINDS (site/src/SXC1/Exercise/Engine.hs, do not change its shape):
    data ProgressEvent = ProgressEvent
      { peDeck :: !DeckId, peExercise :: !ExId, pePrompt :: Maybe PromptId
      , peKind :: !Kind, peOutcome :: !Outcome, peAttempt :: !Int
      , peRevealed :: !Bool, peHints :: !Int
      , peElapsed :: !Int        -- ms on this prompt, MONOTONIC
      , peAt :: !Integer }       -- wall-clock epoch ms; M3 schedules on dates
    data ProgressSink = ProgressSink
      { sinkRecord :: ProgressEvent -> IO (), sinkLoad :: IO [ProgressEvent] }
    data Outcome = Correct | Incorrect | Skipped | Completed
`PromptId` is `<exercise-id>#<1-based index>` (`SXC1.Exercise.Types.promptIdFor`) and
is the key a learner's saved progress and spaced-repetition schedule hang off.
M2 ships an in-memory sink in site/app/Main.hs (`mkProgressSink`, an IORef capped at
200 events, mirrored into the Model as `mEventLog` and rendered into
`#sxc1-event-log`). M3 binds it to localStorage. THE SINK INTERFACE DOES NOT CHANGE.

SCOPE GUARDRAIL (owner addendum, 2026-08-07). M3 adds a persistent "JA-first"
READER preference: when on, the manual reader leads with the original Japanese page
image and English becomes the toggle, remembered across visits. IT IS A READER
PREFERENCE AND NOTHING ELSE. The trainer stays English -- no exercise translation,
no i18n framework, no string catalogue, no second content pipeline. The default is
OFF, which is a safety property: a fresh profile must behave byte-identically to
today, so every existing M1/M2 browser assertion is untouched.

PRIVACY. Everything stays in the browser. No network writes, no analytics, no
telemetry, no remote fonts. The only way progress moves between devices is the
learner copying an export blob by hand.

HOUSE VERIFICATION STANDARDS (this project has been through five adversarial gate
rounds; these are the rules those rounds produced):
  1. Every check must be FALSIFIABLE. Before you claim a check works, SABOTAGE the
     thing it checks and show it goes red, then restore. Record the exact mutation
     and the exact failure message in your final report. A check nobody has seen
     fail is not evidence.
  2. NO VACUOUS CHECKS. An assertion that passes when the thing under test is absent
     is worse than no assertion. Assert on identity and value, not on presence:
     "the decoded record count equals the number of graded prompts", never "the key
     is non-empty".
  3. NO TIMING-WINDOW INFERENCE WHERE OBSERVABILITY IS POSSIBLE. If you can read the
     state, read the state. If you must wait, poll to a settled condition with an
     explicit budget and fail with "X never became true within N ms" -- never sample
     once and hope.
  4. A CHECK THAT COUNTS MUST COUNT INDEPENDENTLY. Re-deriving a number with the
     same implementation you are checking is one implementation checked twice, not
     agreement. Re-derive from disk, in a different language, where you can.
  5. Grep-based invariants are anchored to non-comment lines (`^[^-]*...`) and are
     case-insensitive where the real API's casing could defeat them.
  6. Never weaken, skip or delete an existing check to make your work pass.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO: touch a path you do not own (another agent owns it and is
working in parallel); edit `WASM_GZIP_CEILING_BYTES`; add a new skip axis to
check-site.sh; enable build-site.sh --optimize; import `Miso.Storage` anywhere
except the one module explicitly permitted; commit; push; or edit anything under
briefs/ or PLAN.md.

FINAL REPORT. End with: what you changed and why; every measurement you took
(especially `gzip -c site/public/app.wasm | wc -c`); every sabotage you ran with its
exact mutation and the exact red output; anything you could not do and why. Report
honestly -- a known gap is a finding, a hidden gap is a defect.

tasks.prompt:
=== SHARED CONTEXT (identical in every M3 task prompt; read it all) ===

PROJECT. SXC-1 Trainer: an interactive training course for the Casio SXC-1 sampler,
written entirely in Haskell (Miso + GHC WASM), compiled to WebAssembly, served as
static files from GitHub Pages. Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1.
No backend, no network writes, no analytics. The tree is at tag `m2`: the manual
reader (M1) and the exercise engine (M2) are shipped and gate-cleared.

BUILD / CHECK.
  . "$HOME/.ghc-wasm/env"                       # activates the toolchain
  cd /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site
  wasm32-wasi-cabal build -j2 exe:app           # SXC1_JOBS>2 can OOM this machine
  ./scripts/build-site.sh                       # assembles site/public/
  ./scripts/check-site.sh                       # the full gate suite
Run checker binaries with `wasm-run.mjs <binary> <args>` after sourcing the env.
`wasm-run.mjs` is on PATH from the toolchain env; the absolute path is
$HOME/.ghc-wasm/wasm-run/bin/wasm-run.mjs.

THE SIZE CEILING IS THE DEFINING CONSTRAINT OF M3.
`scripts/check-site.sh` carries `WASM_GZIP_CEILING_BYTES=1000000` and fails the
build if `gzip -c site/public/app.wasm | wc -c` reaches it. M2 shipped at 988,367
bytes -- 11,633 bytes of headroom. **NO M3 TASK MAY EDIT THAT CONSTANT.** Raising a
tripwire instead of fitting under it is a failure mode this project has been burned
by twice; the ceiling is a coordinator decision at a gate, never a task's.

Measured budget facts (from the M3 designer's probes; see briefs/M3-plan.md
appendix -- these are measurements, not estimates):
  * splitting the validating parser out of exe:app saves 45,878 gzip bytes
  * INDEX-driven compile-time embedding saves a further 3,879
  * the M3 progress engine costs +34,123 for ~530 app-linked lines (~64 B/line)
  * embedded .ex.md content costs 0.3456 gzip bytes per raw byte
Each task carries its own descending byte budget in its verify commands. If you
cannot fit, STOP AND REPORT -- do not enable --optimize, do not edit the ceiling,
do not delete checks.

CODE-SIZE LADDER (inherited from M2, still binding on anything linked into exe:app):
derive `Eq` only on wide record/sum types -- NO derived `Show` (hand-write the small
renderer a diagnostic needs anyway); reuse `SXC1.Content.Stats.jsonEscape` and
`Exercises.Corpus`'s jStr/jArr/jInt/jInteger/jKV/jObj/jBool combinators rather than
writing a second JSON encoder; keep `-O1`; never pass `--optimize` to build-site.sh.
There is no `-split-sections` in the cabal file, so a module links as ONE ATOMIC
UNIT: importing any name from a module drags in that module's every other
definition, including derived instances on types you never touch. That single fact
is why the reader/validator split exists.

CLOCK DISCIPLINE (from the M2 gate, non-negotiable and extended by M3).
`SXC1.Exercise.Engine` defines `newtype MonoMs = MonoMs Integer` and
`newtype WallMs = WallMs Integer` -- deliberately distinct newtypes over the same
representation so the two clock domains cannot be swapped at a call site. MonoMs is
monotonic and is the ONLY thing safe to subtract for a duration; WallMs is a
wall-clock epoch reading and is the only thing safe to schedule a date against.
Neither derives Num or Ord, so they cannot be arithmetic-mixed. Pure code NEVER
reads a clock: every clock reading is taken at the IO boundary and passed in as an
argument. M3 extends this -- nothing under `SXC1.Progress.*` may read a clock,
import Miso, or perform IO.

THE M2 CONTRACT M3 BINDS (site/src/SXC1/Exercise/Engine.hs, do not change its shape):
    data ProgressEvent = ProgressEvent
      { peDeck :: !DeckId, peExercise :: !ExId, pePrompt :: Maybe PromptId
      , peKind :: !Kind, peOutcome :: !Outcome, peAttempt :: !Int
      , peRevealed :: !Bool, peHints :: !Int
      , peElapsed :: !Int        -- ms on this prompt, MONOTONIC
      , peAt :: !Integer }       -- wall-clock epoch ms; M3 schedules on dates
    data ProgressSink = ProgressSink
      { sinkRecord :: ProgressEvent -> IO (), sinkLoad :: IO [ProgressEvent] }
    data Outcome = Correct | Incorrect | Skipped | Completed
`PromptId` is `<exercise-id>#<1-based index>` (`SXC1.Exercise.Types.promptIdFor`) and
is the key a learner's saved progress and spaced-repetition schedule hang off.
M2 ships an in-memory sink in site/app/Main.hs (`mkProgressSink`, an IORef capped at
200 events, mirrored into the Model as `mEventLog` and rendered into
`#sxc1-event-log`). M3 binds it to localStorage. THE SINK INTERFACE DOES NOT CHANGE.

SCOPE GUARDRAIL (owner addendum, 2026-08-07). M3 adds a persistent "JA-first"
READER preference: when on, the manual reader leads with the original Japanese page
image and English becomes the toggle, remembered across visits. IT IS A READER
PREFERENCE AND NOTHING ELSE. The trainer stays English -- no exercise translation,
no i18n framework, no string catalogue, no second content pipeline. The default is
OFF, which is a safety property: a fresh profile must behave byte-identically to
today, so every existing M1/M2 browser assertion is untouched.

PRIVACY. Everything stays in the browser. No network writes, no analytics, no
telemetry, no remote fonts. The only way progress moves between devices is the
learner copying an export blob by hand.

HOUSE VERIFICATION STANDARDS (this project has been through five adversarial gate
rounds; these are the rules those rounds produced):
  1. Every check must be FALSIFIABLE. Before you claim a check works, SABOTAGE the
     thing it checks and show it goes red, then restore. Record the exact mutation
     and the exact failure message in your final report. A check nobody has seen
     fail is not evidence.
  2. NO VACUOUS CHECKS. An assertion that passes when the thing under test is absent
     is worse than no assertion. Assert on identity and value, not on presence:
     "the decoded record count equals the number of graded prompts", never "the key
     is non-empty".
  3. NO TIMING-WINDOW INFERENCE WHERE OBSERVABILITY IS POSSIBLE. If you can read the
     state, read the state. If you must wait, poll to a settled condition with an
     explicit budget and fail with "X never became true within N ms" -- never sample
     once and hope.
  4. A CHECK THAT COUNTS MUST COUNT INDEPENDENTLY. Re-deriving a number with the
     same implementation you are checking is one implementation checked twice, not
     agreement. Re-derive from disk, in a different language, where you can.
  5. Grep-based invariants are anchored to non-comment lines (`^[^-]*...`) and are
     case-insensitive where the real API's casing could defeat them.
  6. Never weaken, skip or delete an existing check to make your work pass.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO: touch a path you do not own (another agent owns it and is
working in parallel); edit `WASM_GZIP_CEILING_BYTES`; add a new skip axis to
check-site.sh; enable build-site.sh --optimize; import `Miso.Storage` anywhere
except the one module explicitly permitted; commit; push; or edit anything under
briefs/ or PLAN.md.

FINAL REPORT. End with: what you changed and why; every measurement you took
(especially `gzip -c site/public/app.wasm | wc -c`); every sabotage you ran with its
exact mutation and the exact red output; anything you could not do and why. Report
honestly -- a known gap is a finding, a hidden gap is a defect.
=== END SHARED CONTEXT ===

=== YOUR TASK: wave 2 of M3 -- the pure progress core ===

You own exactly:
    site/src/SXC1/Progress/       (Types.hs, Scheduler.hs, Codec.hs -- replace the
                                   wave-1 stubs wholesale)
    site/test/CheckProgress.hs    (replace the wave-1 stub wholesale)
The cabal file ALREADY declares these modules and `executable progress-check`
(wave 1 did it). DO NOT EDIT site/sxc1-trainer.cabal.

NOTHING IN THIS TASK PERFORMS IO, IMPORTS MISO, OR READS A CLOCK. That is the whole
point: the scheduler is a pure function of (event history) and is therefore exactly
replayable and unit-testable without a browser. If you find yourself wanting the
current time, you want an argument instead.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
(1) SXC1.Progress.Types
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    data Grade = GAgain | GHard | GGood | GEasy   deriving (Eq, Show, Enum, Bounded)
    newtype DayNum = DayNum { unDayNum :: Int }   deriving (Eq, Ord, Show)
    data Rec = Rec { rcReps, rcLapses, rcEase, rcInterval :: !Int
                   , rcDue, rcLastSeen :: !DayNum, rcSeen :: !Int }  deriving Eq
    data SchemaVersion = SchemaVersion !Int       deriving (Eq, Show)
    data ProgressState = ProgressState
      { psVersion :: !SchemaVersion
      , psRecs :: !(Map Text Rec)      -- keyed by PromptId TEXT
      , psDone :: !(Map Text Int)      -- exercise id -> completions
      , psStreakDay :: !DayNum, psStreakLen :: !Int, psFirstDay :: !DayNum }
      deriving Eq
    emptyProgress :: ProgressState
    dayOf :: Integer -> DayNum         -- wall epoch ms -> UTC day; integer division;
                                       -- <= 0 maps to DayNum 0
    gradeOfOutcome :: Outcome -> Int -> Bool -> Int -> Grade
`gradeOfOutcome outcome attempt revealed hints` is THE ONLY PLACE an `Outcome` is
interpreted -- the scheduler must never inspect one. Mapping:
    Incorrect -> GAgain;  Skipped -> GAgain;  Completed -> GGood
    Correct & revealed        -> GHard
    Correct & attempt >= 2    -> GHard
    Correct & hints > 0       -> GGood
    Correct, first try, clean -> GEasy
Derive Eq only on Rec and ProgressState (size discipline). Day granularity is
deliberate: a learner who studies at 23:59 and again at 00:01 must not be charged a
whole interval.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
(2) SXC1.Progress.Scheduler -- integer SM-2
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
NO FLOATING POINT ANYWHERE. This is not style. `Int` is 32-bit on wasm32 (M1's
NEW8), the scheduler runs in the browser and is tested in a separate binary, and a
stored schedule must replay to bit-identical records forever on any target. A Double
in a replay path puts that at risk. The ease factor is therefore carried as
MILLI-UNITS in an Int: 2500 means 2.5.

Ease bounds: min 1300, max 3000, default 2500. SM-2's update
`EF' = EF + (0.1 - (5-q)*(0.08 + (5-q)*0.02))` for the four grades at q = 2,3,4,5
evaluates EXACTLY to these deltas -- use them as literals, do not compute them:
    GAgain -> -320    GHard -> -140    GGood -> 0    GEasy -> +100
    nextIntervalDays :: Rec -> Grade -> Int
      GAgain                      -> 0
      GHard,  reps == 0           -> 1
      GHard,  otherwise           -> clamp1_180 (interval * 12 `div` 10)
      GGood,  reps == 0           -> 1
      GGood,  reps == 1           -> 3
      GGood,  otherwise           -> clamp1_180 (interval * ease `div` 1000)
      GEasy,  reps == 0           -> 2
      GEasy,  reps == 1           -> 5
      GEasy,  otherwise           -> clamp1_180 (interval * ease * 13 `div` 10000)
where clamp1_180 x = max 1 (min 180 x). The 180-day cap is deliberate: this is a
device-training course, and an uncapped SM-2 curve schedules items past the point
where the learner still owns the hardware.
On grading: reps' = 0 if GAgain else reps+1; lapses' = lapses+1 iff GAgain AND
reps > 0; due' = today + interval'; lastSeen' = today; seen' = seen+1.

    applyEvent  :: ProgressEvent -> ProgressState -> ProgressState
    applyEvents :: [ProgressEvent] -> ProgressState -> ProgressState
`applyEvent` TAKES NO CLOCK ARGUMENT AT ALL. The day comes from the event's own
`peAt` via `dayOf`. An event with `pePrompt = Nothing` and `peOutcome = Completed`
increments `psDone` for its exercise and touches nothing else.

Streak rule (`bumpStreak today lastDay len`): first ever -> (today, 1); same day ->
unchanged, floor 1; exactly next day -> len+1; a later day after a gap -> 1; a day
BEFORE the recorded one (a backwards clock, or an imported history) -> unchanged.
Never advances and never shortens on a backwards day.

    reviewQueue :: DayNum -> ProgressState -> [(Text, Rec)]
Every prompt whose `rcDue <= today`, sorted by `(unDayNum rcDue, promptId)` -- a
TOTAL order, so the queue can never depend on Map iteration order changing under a
different key set. Also `dueCount` and `retention` (integer percentage of known
items not currently overdue; 0 when there are none).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
(3) SXC1.Progress.Codec -- the versioned wire format and the migration mechanism
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    currentSchema :: Int   -- 1
Wire format, line-oriented, tab-separated, ASCII, NOT JSON (the app has a JSON
encoder and no decoder; every field here is an Int or an already-slug-shaped id, so
there is nothing to quote and nothing to escape, and the reader is a splitOn fold):
    SXC1PROGRESS <TAB> <schemaVersion>
    M <TAB> streakDay <TAB> streakLen <TAB> firstDay
    R <TAB> promptId <TAB> reps <TAB> lapses <TAB> ease <TAB> interval <TAB> due <TAB> lastSeen <TAB> seen
    D <TAB> exerciseId <TAB> completions
UNKNOWN LEADING TAGS ARE SKIPPED, NOT REJECTED -- a newer schema's extra record types
must degrade to "ignored" in an older build rather than discarding a history. Parse
integers with `SXC1.Route.parseDigits` (never `read`).

    data DecodeResult = DecodeEmpty | DecodeOk !ProgressState | DecodeCorrupt !Text
THE THREE-WAY SPLIT IS LOAD-BEARING, DO NOT COLLAPSE IT TO Maybe. A learner's
history is the one thing in this app that cannot be regenerated, so "I could not
read it" must never be indistinguishable from "there was nothing to read" -- a
`Maybe` would let the first case be overwritten by the next write. `DecodeCorrupt`
carries a human-readable reason. A blob whose version EXCEEDS `currentSchema` is
`DecodeCorrupt`, never read as current.

    encodeState :: ProgressState -> Text
    decodeState :: Text -> DecodeResult
    migrateWith :: (Int -> Maybe (ProgressState -> ProgressState))
                -> Int -> ProgressState -> DecodeResult
    migrate     :: Int -> ProgressState -> DecodeResult   -- = migrateWith productionSteps
`migrateWith stepTable v st` walks v -> v+1 -> ... -> currentSchema, applying
`stepTable n` at each hop and returning `DecodeCorrupt` if a hop has no step.
`productionSteps _ = Nothing` at v1 (there is nothing to migrate from yet).
THE PARAMETERISATION IS THE WHOLE POINT AND YOU MUST NOT INLINE IT AWAY: at v1 a
migration test would otherwise be vacuous. Your self-test calls `migrateWith` with a
TEST-ONLY step table and a synthetic SCHEMA-0 blob and asserts the chain actually
transformed the state. That way the mechanism is exercised now, and adding v2 later
is a one-line change to something already tested rather than the invention of a
mechanism under pressure.

THE READER-PREFERENCE BLOB (owner addendum) -- a SECOND key, a SHARED reader:
    SXC1PREFS <TAB> <schemaVersion>
    P <TAB> jaFirst <TAB> 0|1
    data Prefs = Prefs { prfJaFirst :: !Bool } deriving Eq
    defaultPrefs :: Prefs                 -- jaFirst = False
    prefsSchema  :: Int                   -- 1
    encodePrefs  :: Prefs -> Text
    decodePrefs  :: Text -> Prefs
COST CONSTRAINT, AND IT IS THE POINT OF THIS PARAGRAPH: the designer measured a
naive implementation (second magic string, SECOND DECODER, second store pair) at
+5,936 gzip bytes, which is enough to push workstream B over the ceiling on its own.
FACTOR OUT ONE SHARED line-oriented `tag/key/value` splitter and use it for BOTH
blobs. The prefs half must add a magic string, a two-field record and an encoder --
NOT a second parser. Budget: 3,000 bytes for the whole preference feature including
wave 3's store bindings.
TWO DELIBERATE ASYMMETRIES WITH `decodeState`, both of which you must implement and
document in the Haddock:
  * `decodePrefs` returns a `Prefs`, never a `DecodeResult`. An unreadable preference
    blob FALLS BACK TO DEFAULTS and may be overwritten, because a preference is
    trivially regenerable -- the learner flips one switch. An unreadable PROGRESS
    blob is never overwritten, because a history cannot be regenerated.
  * It is a SEPARATE KEY, not a field on `ProgressState`, for the same reason: a
    corrupt progress blob puts the app into read-only progress mode, and a reading
    preference must still be settable in that state. Wiping progress must not wipe
    the reading preference.
A prefs blob whose version exceeds `prefsSchema`, or whose header is missing, yields
`defaultPrefs`. Unknown `P` names are skipped, same degradation rule as the progress
blob.

Export / import envelope:
    exportBlob :: Text -> ProgressState -> Text
    importBlob :: Text -> DecodeResult
`exportBlob` emits
{"format":"sxc1-progress","schema":<n>,"exportedAt":"<stamp>","payload":"<wire text>"}
with the payload being the SAME wire text `encodeState` produces -- one format to
keep correct, and the importer needs only enough JSON to pull one string field out,
not a general parser. `importBlob` accepts EITHER the envelope OR a bare wire blob
(text starting with `SXC1PROGRESS`), so a learner who copies only the inner text
still recovers their history. Escape `"`, `\`, newline, tab and CR on the way out
and unescape them on the way back.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
(4) exe:progress-check  (site/test/CheckProgress.hs)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Follow the shape of the existing `site/test/CheckExercises.hs`: numbered assertion
groups, an `assertionLabel :: Int -> String`, a loop over the group range, a
`groupsOk` accumulator requiring EVERY GROUP TO BE NON-EMPTY as well as passing
(this is M1's NEW12 -- an empty assertion group printing FAIL but exiting 0 is a bug
class this project has already been bitten by; do not reproduce it from birth), and
a non-zero exit on any failure. Support `--self-test` and a `--replay <file>` mode
that reads a `#sxc1-event-log` JSON array and prints the resulting `encodeState`
(the designer will use it at sign-off to compare against a real browser's stored
blob).

Required assertion groups, at minimum:
  1. `nextIntervalDays` pinned against a hand-computed table covering all four
     grades at reps 0, 1 and >=2, including both clamp boundaries (1 and 180) and
     the ease clamp at 1300 and 3000.
  2. `gradeOfOutcome` exhaustive over the mapping above, including that `Correct`
     with `revealed = True` is GHard even on attempt 1.
  3. Replay determinism: a fixed event list folded through `applyEvents` twice gives
     equal states; and `decodeState (encodeState s) == DecodeOk s` for a non-trivial
     `s` (round trip).
  4. `reviewQueue` total order: two records with the SAME due day come back in
     prompt-id order, and the result is invariant under insertion order.
  5. Streak rule: same day, next day, gap, and BACKWARDS day.
  6. `dayOf`: 0 and negatives map to DayNum 0; a known epoch-ms value maps to the
     hand-computed day; two times on the same UTC day map equal.
  7. Codec robustness: missing header -> DecodeCorrupt; empty/whitespace ->
     DecodeEmpty; version 0 and version currentSchema+1 -> DecodeCorrupt; an
     UNKNOWN record tag is skipped and the rest of the blob still decodes; a
     truncated `R` line is skipped without losing the other records.
  8. Migration mechanism: `migrateWith` with a test step table transforms a
     synthetic schema-0 blob's state, AND a control proving the chain is really
     running (a step table missing a hop yields DecodeCorrupt).
  9. Export/import: envelope round trip; bare-wire-blob import; a payload containing
     tabs, newlines and double quotes survives escaping.
 10. Prefs codec: round trip; a missing/short header yields defaults; a version above
     `prefsSchema` yields defaults; an unknown `P` name is skipped while `jaFirst`
     still decodes; and `decodePrefs ""` is `defaultPrefs` with `jaFirst = False`
     (the default-OFF safety property the whole feature rests on).
 11. Determinism guard: assert by source inspection in your report (and state it in
     the module Haddock) that no module under SXC1.Progress imports Miso, performs
     IO, or reads a clock.

SABOTAGE SWEEP (run every one, record the exact red output, then restore):
  * change one `easeDelta` literal -> group 1 fails;
  * make `reviewQueue` sort by due day only -> group 4 fails;
  * make `bumpStreak` advance on a backwards day -> group 5 fails;
  * make `decodeState` return `DecodeEmpty` for a bad header -> group 7 fails;
  * make `migrateWith` return `DecodeOk` without applying steps -> group 8 fails;
  * flip `defaultPrefs` to `jaFirst = True` -> group 10 fails (this is the control
    that keeps the default-OFF safety property honest);
  * make `applyEvent` take a `now` argument and use it -> the module stops compiling
    against its own callers, which is the point; note it in the report.

`wasm-run.mjs` is on PATH from the toolchain env; the absolute path is
$HOME/.ghc-wasm/wasm-run/bin/wasm-run.mjs.

`scripts/check-site.sh` carries `WASM_GZIP_CEILING_BYTES=1000000` and fails the
build if `gzip -c site/public/app.wasm | wc -c` reaches it. M2 shipped at 988,367

do not delete checks.

CODE-SIZE LADDER (inherited from M2, still binding on anything linked into exe:app):

CLOCK DISCIPLINE (from the M2 gate, non-negotiable and extended by M3).
`SXC1.Exercise.Engine` defines `newtype MonoMs = MonoMs Integer` and
`newtype WallMs = WallMs Integer` -- deliberately distinct newtypes over the same
representation so the two clock domains cannot be swapped at a call site. MonoMs is
monotonic and is the ONLY thing safe to subtract for a duration; WallMs is a
wall-clock epoch reading and is the only thing safe to schedule a date against.
Neither derives Num or Ord, so they cannot be arithmetic-mixed. Pure code NEVER
reads a clock: every clock reading is taken at the IO boundary and passed in as an
argument. M3 extends this -- nothing under `SXC1.Progress.*` may read a clock,
import Miso, or perform IO.

PROJECT. SXC-1 Trainer: an interactive training course for the Casio SXC-1 sampler,
written entirely in Haskell (Miso + GHC WASM), compiled to WebAssembly, served as
static files from GitHub Pages. Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1.
No backend, no network writes, no analytics. The tree is at tag `m2`: the manual
reader (M1) and the exercise engine (M2) are shipped and gate-cleared.

BUILD / CHECK.
  . "$HOME/.ghc-wasm/env"                       # activates the toolchain
  cd /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site
  wasm32-wasi-cabal build -j2 exe:app           # SXC1_JOBS>2 can OOM this machine
  ./scripts/build-site.sh                       # assembles site/public/
  ./scripts/check-site.sh                       # the full gate suite
Run checker binaries with `wasm-run.mjs <binary> <args>` after sourcing the env.
`wasm-run.mjs` is on PATH from the toolchain env; the absolute path is
$HOME/.ghc-wasm/wasm-run/bin/wasm-run.mjs.

THE SIZE CEILING IS THE DEFINING CONSTRAINT OF M3.
`scripts/check-site.sh` carries `WASM_GZIP_CEILING_BYTES=1000000` and fails the
build if `gzip -c site/public/app.wasm | wc -c` reaches it. M2 shipped at 988,367
bytes -- 11,633 bytes of headroom. **NO M3 TASK MAY EDIT THAT CONSTANT.** Raising a
tripwire instead of fitting under it is a failure mode this project has been burned
by twice; the ceiling is a coordinator decision at a gate, never a task's.

Measured budget facts (from the M3 designer's probes; see briefs/M3-plan.md
appendix -- these are measurements, not estimates):
  * splitting the validating parser out of exe:app saves 45,878 gzip bytes
  * INDEX-driven compile-time embedding saves a further 3,879
  * the M3 progress engine costs +34,123 for ~530 app-linked lines (~64 B/line)
  * embedded .ex.md content costs 0.3456 gzip bytes per raw byte
Each task carries its own descending byte budget in its verify commands. If you
cannot fit, STOP AND REPORT -- do not enable --optimize, do not edit the ceiling,
do not delete checks.

renderer a diagnostic needs anyway); reuse `SXC1.Content.Stats.jsonEscape` and

writing a second JSON encoder; keep `-O1`; never pass `--optimize` to build-site.sh.

UNIT: importing any name from a module drags in that module's every other
definition, including derived instances on types you never touch. That single fact
is why the reader/validator split exists.

CLOCK DISCIPLINE (from the M2 gate, non-negotiable and extended by M3).
`SXC1.Exercise.Engine` defines `newtype MonoMs = MonoMs Integer` and
`newtype WallMs = WallMs Integer` -- deliberately distinct newtypes over the same
representation so the two clock domains cannot be swapped at a call site. MonoMs is
monotonic and is the ONLY thing safe to subtract for a duration; WallMs is a
wall-clock epoch reading and is the only thing safe to schedule a date against.
Neither derives Num or Ord, so they cannot be arithmetic-mixed. Pure code NEVER
reads a clock: every clock reading is taken at the IO boundary and passed in as an
argument. M3 extends this -- nothing under `SXC1.Progress.*` may read a clock,
import Miso, or perform IO.

    data ProgressEvent = ProgressEvent
      { peDeck :: !DeckId, peExercise :: !ExId, pePrompt :: Maybe PromptId
      , peKind :: !Kind, peOutcome :: !Outcome, peAttempt :: !Int
      , peRevealed :: !Bool, peHints :: !Int
      , peElapsed :: !Int        -- ms on this prompt, MONOTONIC
      , peAt :: !Integer }       -- wall-clock epoch ms; M3 schedules on dates

    data Outcome = Correct | Incorrect | Skipped | Completed

is the key a learner's saved progress and spaced-repetition schedule hang off.

200 events, mirrored into the Model as `mEventLog` and rendered into
`#sxc1-event-log`). M3 binds it to localStorage. THE SINK INTERFACE DOES NOT CHANGE.

READER preference: when on, the manual reader leads with the original Japanese page
image and English becomes the toggle, remembered across visits. IT IS A READER

exact mutation and the exact red output; anything you could not do and why. Report
honestly -- a known gap is a finding, a hidden gap is a defect.

Nothing else. In particular you do NOT own site/ or content/.

drives real headless Chrome over CDP. Both are large and battle-tested across five
adversarial gate rounds. READ THEM BEFORE YOU CHANGE THEM, and preserve every
existing check.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
(1) PERSISTENCE ASSERTIONS -- the milestone's contract requirement
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Add to browser-check.mjs, running against the real built site:

  A. ANSWER -> RELOAD -> STATE SURVIVES.
     Cold-load a fixture exercise, answer it first-try correct, then reload the page
     and assert the state came back.
     THIS MUST NOT BE "the key is non-empty". Assert on IDENTITY AND VALUE: the
     `#sxc1-progress` payload's `records` count equals the number of graded prompts,
     the specific `PromptId` appears in the stored blob, and its interval is the
     value the scheduler specifies for a clean first-try correct answer (a fresh
     `GEasy` at reps 0 gives interval 2, due = today + 2). A check that would pass
     against an empty store is worse than no check.

  B. EXPORT -> WIPE -> IMPORT -> STATE SURVIVES.
     Read `#sxc1-export-blob`, click wipe and its confirm, ASSERT THE STORE IS
     GENUINELY EMPTY IN BETWEEN (otherwise the import proves nothing), paste the
     blob into `#sxc1-import-input`, commit, and assert the same record identity and
     values as before the wipe.

  C. NEGATIVE CONTROLS, each of which must be shown to fail when the behaviour it
     guards is broken:
       c1. A hand-corrupted `sxc1.progress` value: `#sxc1-corrupt-banner` appears,
           AND THE KEY IS STILL PRESENT AND UNCHANGED after a reload and after
           answering another question. This is the never-overwrite rule.
       c2. A fresh browser profile shows `#sxc1-progress` with `records: 0` before
           any answer -- so "state survives" cannot pass on a stale profile.
       c3. Storage refused: assert the app still boots and reports
           `available: false` rather than crashing. (Drive this however Chrome lets
           you; if you cannot make Chrome refuse storage reliably, say so plainly in
           your report and assert the code path some other way rather than shipping
           a check that silently never runs.)
     Add every new assertion NAME to browser-check.mjs's own `--self-test`
     expected-failure fixture, following the existing pattern, so each assertion is
     proven able to fail.

  D. JA-FIRST: SET -> RELOAD -> STILL JA-FIRST (owner addendum). Click
     `#btn-ja-first`, reload, and assert BOTH halves: the stored `sxc1.prefs` value
     AND the rendered order (the original-page panel leads on a manual page).
     NEGATIVE CONTROLS, all three required:
       d1. A FRESH PROFILE IS NOT JA-FIRST -- otherwise the assertion could pass
           vacuously against a default that happens to match.
       d2. Wiping progress does NOT clear the reading preference (they are separate
           keys on purpose).
       d3. With JA-first ON, an explicit `#btn-ja-toggle` click genuinely hides the
           panel AND it stays hidden until the learner navigates to a different
           page. The preference must not fight the toggle; this is the most likely
           way for the feature to be implemented wrongly.
  E. Also assert the review-queue badge count equals the payload's `due`, and that
     a deck card's `data-tier` matches the deck's `tier:`.

Wave 4's final report lists the exact DOM ids it shipped. Use that list.

(2) FIX THE #sxc1-prompt-baseline RACE  (a defect the M3 designer reproduced)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
The cold-load assertion `#sxc1-prompt-baseline is a positive number` reads the
element ONCE, immediately after boot. Measured: it failed 1 run in 7 against a
faster-booting artifact and 0 in 5 against a slower one; five subsequent runs of the
SAME faster artifact passed. The mount -> SetRoute -> beginIfNeeded -> ExBatch Begin
round trip has not necessarily flushed when the read happens, and `null` from a
not-yet-flushed Begin is indistinguishable from `null` from the LOST Begin the
assertion exists to catch.
FIX: poll to a settled condition with an explicit budget and fail with
"baseline never became positive within N ms" rather than sampling a race. The
assertion must still fail when the mount-time Begin is genuinely removed -- prove
that, by removing it in a scratch copy of the tree if you can build one, or by
pointing the check at a stubbed payload. A check that can go red for timing reasons
teaches everyone to re-run it, which is how a real regression gets waved through.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

deck/id/steps/hasVerify and lookup deck/id/targetPage. A hand-supplied or stale
fixture missing drill.citeSlug/citePage or lookup.targetSlug passes upfront
validation, then produces #/m/undefined/... expectations and fails later with
misleading browser output." Add `citeSlug` and `citePage` to the drill schema and
`targetSlug` to the lookup schema, so the stated fail-fast contract holds. Prove it
by feeding a fixture missing each field and confirming the run exits before a
browser is launched.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
(4) THE SIZE LEDGER
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
The M3 designer measured that the full 435-exercise course cannot fit under the
1,000,000-byte ceiling as an embedded corpus: the coefficient is 0.3456 gzip bytes
per raw byte of `.ex.md`, and the projected end state is roughly 1,123,000. That is
a coordinator decision, NOT yours -- you must not raise the ceiling and must not
enable --optimize by default.
What you build is the instrument that keeps the decision from being rediscovered at
deck 40: `check-site.sh` records, on every run, the measured `app.wasm` gzip size,
the measured total raw bytes of `content/exercises/*.ex.md`, and a PROJECTION for a
435-exercise corpus using the committed 0.3456 coefficient, appending a row to
`state/size-ledger.tsv` (state/ is gitignored -- create it if absent). The check
FAILS if it cannot compute or record those three numbers. IT MUST NOT FAIL merely
because the projection exceeds the ceiling -- report that loudly as an `info`/
warning line naming the shortfall. Add the coefficient as a named, commented
constant so a future measurement can replace it deliberately.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
(5) check-site.sh --optimized  (BUILD THE LEVER, DO NOT PULL IT)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Add a `--optimized` flag that builds, runs `wasm-opt -all -O2` then
`wasm-tools strip` (post-link.mjs FIRST -- stripping removes the custom section it
reads), and then runs THE ENTIRE EXISTING SUITE against that artifact, reporting its
gzip size alongside the unoptimized one. The default behaviour must be completely
unchanged, and `build-site.sh --optimize` must stay off by default.
Rationale you should know: the designer measured this lever at 169-179 KB and could
not make it miscompile -- `exercise-check --self-test` gave 113/113 with
byte-identical output, and the optimized real app passed 70/70 browser assertions
across six runs. The point of the flag is that the tested artifact and the shipped
artifact stop being different objects IF the coordinator later adopts it. Adopting
it is not your call.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
(6) WIRE THE TWO NEW BINARIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
`build-site.sh` line ~90 builds `exe:app exe:content-check exe:exercise-check`;
append `exe:progress-check exe:registry-check`. Run both in check-site.sh on the
EXISTING content axis -- ADD NO NEW SKIP FLAG (M2's ruling: one fewer switch is one
fewer route to `result=complete` without having checked), and make sure every check

`setLocalStorage`, so a case-sensitive search for `localStorage` would miss it.

them, so no labelled group goes unchecked and no group goes unlabelled.
